1.explanation: The error stack points at Cascader.setCache and Cascader.updateCache: these methods iterate the passed dataSource and add internal properties (e.g. ‘value’, ‘pos’, map entries) directly onto each node. Because immer froze the original objects, this mutation throws. Similarly, CascaderSelect’s updateCache mutates the user‐provided dataSource for caching. To fix the bug, both updateCache/setCache implementations should clone each item (or work on an internal copy) rather than mutating the original dataSource array’s objects.
1.bug_scenario: When using <CascaderSelect> with an immer‐produced (auto‐frozen) dataSource, the component’s internal cache routines attempt to mutate the user’s data objects. The screenshot shows a “Cannot add property value, object is not extensible” error in cascader.js when the frozen items are looped over and augmented. In other words, CascaderSelect/Cascader should never modify the original dataSource but they do – causing failures under immutable patterns like immer.

2.explanation: The Cascader class is responsible for taking the user’s dataSource array and building internal look-up maps (v2n, p2n) by traversing the tree. In its updateCache method it loops over each node and calls an internal setCache function, which writes metadata properties directly onto the passed objects (pos, value, children, etc.). When the input objects come from an immer draft with autoFreeze enabled, they are non-extensible, so any mutation (adding a property) throws an error. These two methods thus represent the core bug: they mutate user data instead of working on a clone.
2.bug_scenario: When using CascaderSelect with an immer-produced (and auto-frozen) data array, the console shows “Uncaught TypeError: Cannot add property value, object is not extensible” in cascader.js. The error occurs inside the Cascader component’s cache-building logic, which is mutating the user’s frozen dataSource by attaching internal metadata (like pos, key, etc.) onto the original node objects.
